messages.text: wait, before i go to bed. do we want to run that quick test on the 4b model? just to see if it's fast enough for the demo latency budget
honestly? i'd rather not risk it right now. our p95 is finally under 1s with the 27b model and i don't want to destabilize that a week before the hackathon
fair. but for the paper, having a 'smaller is faster' data point looks good. plus if we can get 3x speedup without losing accuracy, it's a strong argument for local inference feasibility
okay, but only if we use the same 40 test cases we used for the 27b eval. i'll pull the dataset and run the benchmark on my end tonight so it doesn't block your sleep
perfect. just make sure you disable reasoning_effort for both, otherwise the timing comparison is useless. i hit that empty string bug earlier and it took me 20 mins to realize why
noted. running it now... give me 15 mins while i set up the docker container for the 4b model
ok, results are in. 4b is actually significantly faster: avg 0.5s vs 1.8s for the 27b. that's a 3.6x speedup
whoa, okay that's actually better than i expected. how did the accuracy look?
mixed bag. it agreed with the 27b on 37 out of 40 valid cases. but on the junk string test, it accepted 2 out of 10 garbage entries as valid concepts. the 27b rejected all 10

hmm. so it's faster but less conservative. i'd say we stick with 27b for production adjudication, but we definitely include this trade-off table in the paper. it shows we considered the small model option
agreed. i'll write up the numbers and add a note about the junk acceptance rate. good to have that decision documented before we submit the abstract
